title: The Pirate of the Southern Skies
caption: The Skull and Crossbones Nebula, NGC 2467, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 2467 · constellation Puppis · about 4500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Dust, gas and bright young stars seem to form a grinning skull in this picture of NGC 2467, a nebula nicknamed the Skull and Crossbones. It is an active star-forming region, and the image was captured with the FORS instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope.

In a star-forming region, clouds of gas and dust collapse under gravity to make new stars. Once those stars switch on, their intense light energises the surrounding gas and makes it glow. Here the gas, dust and stars happen to be arranged so that the whole thing suggests a face.

ESO's telescopes are normally busy collecting data for scientific research. Their immense resolving power, though, also makes them well suited to capturing images like this one, which are valued simply for their own beauty.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.21 x 7.41 arcminutes) and distance (4500 light years), the frame spans roughly 9.4 × 9.7 light-years. Its light set out about 4,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image comes from the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, using b, v and R filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter. The colour assigned to each filter is not published.
filters: 440 nm · Optical b (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
557 nm · Optical v (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
655 nm · Optical R (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
656 nm · Optical H-alpha (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
understand.eye: The long exposure and hydrogen-alpha filter bring out faint glowing gas much more clearly than an eye could see it.
